title: Paris 1606 Cistercian post-Canon Ordinary tail and appended Suffragium: complete bounded original-image reading

uses.locus: Printed 197 left Orémus after excluded strict Canon final Amen through main Order closure on 199 right; appended Suffragium on 200 through final Amen; 201 Sanctorale outside.
uses.scope: Complete bounded printed post-Canon tail and appended Suffragium of the Paris 1606 Cistercian missal. It begins with Orémus/Præcéptis on printed p. 197 left, immediately after and excluding the accepted strict Canon’s final Per omnia/Amen. The main Ordinary tail closes on printed p. 199 right with the departure rubric Sicque signans se, & inclinans recedat. The appended Suffragium pro pace Ecclesiastica & temporali on printed p. 200 is included through its final Amen before INCIPIT SANCTORALE on p. 201. The appendix is printed after the main closure but its own rubric assigns recitation after the Canon’s Pater noster; units retain physical source order rather than silently relocating it. This is a bounded composite functional selection, not an assertion of an uninterrupted printed chapter or complete Ordinary. All in-scope prayers, abbreviated incipits, rubrics, response cues, crosses and sung words are included under the disclosed normalization. The prior 7-unit offertory and 35-unit Canon remain unchanged. Whole-Missal and complete-Ordinary text coverage remain partial; no wording or ancestry is inherited.
contrary_findings: The continuing Canon Missæ running head through p.200 does not extend the strict Canon beyond its accepted final Amen on p.197.
The main Order closes on p.199; the p. 200 Suffragium is appended physically but its rubric orders recitation after Pater noster Canonis.
The post-Canon Pater and appendix Pater incipit are distinct source forms; no full text is supplied for the latter.
resolved_readings: pręséntibus and déxterę preserve actual e-cauda; eleíson preserves the printed acute.
All eight raised hook-over-dot signs serialize as disclosed U+2E4E ⹎ mapping without an exact typeface or prosody claim.
quem tam sancta and actual abbreviated endings/incipits retained without familiar Roman replacement.
Detached ink speck before Antequam and INCIPIT catchword excluded as source furniture.
uses.limitations: The separate complete bounded post-Canon tail and appended Suffragium are independently collated in 64 source-order units: Orémus/Præcéptis after the excluded strict Canon final Amen on printed p. 197, the main Order closure on p. 199, and the p. 200 Suffragium through final Amen before Sanctorale p. 201. The appendix is physically printed after the main closure but its own rubric assigns recitation after Pater noster Canonis; it is retained in physical source order. A five-page lossless facsimile retains printed pp. 197–201, with p. 201 outside the constituent as boundary evidence. Earlier offertory and Canon IDs and literal bytes remain unchanged. This complete bounded composite selection does not complete the Ordinary or whole Missal, imply uninterrupted printed chapter divisions, establish monastery reception or supply ancestry.
